video_title: Stephen A. and Pablo Torre Unpack the Kawhi Leonard NBA Scandal

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Pablo Torre on the investigation into Steve Ballmer and Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: This does not happen without a commitment to this sort of work that is on the backs

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: This does not happen without a commitment to this sort of work that is on the backs of sources. In some cases, people, Stephen A., who had to risk what it means when you go up against a guy like Steve Ballmer when you are saying that the story that he wants you to know is not the truth.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: Take us back to over a year ago, Pablo, when you first started reporting on this. Could you alert us to how you first got wind of something like this and what you had to go through in order to get the information that you've acquired in revealing the story?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: We have been in public doing this series for one year exactly today. It has been 365 days, Stephen A., which does not feel coincidental to me that the NBA gave us a year of a 15-part series at this point. But before then, it was months before part one dropped. It was months of investigation. And the thing that really opened the whole doorway to this hidden world in which Steve Ballmer was using, according to the NBA and our reporting, four different partners, business partners, companies, some of them public companies: Dactronics, the scoreboard maker; Aspiration, the tree-planting startup; Locked-in Insurance, the insurance company on the construction of the Intuit Dome; as well as Boingo Wireless, the wireless provider of the Intuit Dome. Four companies all funneling money from Steve Ballmer to Kawhi Leonard to break the rules.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's failed attempt to circumvent the salary cap
quotes.excerpt: This is the story of a smart man in Steve Ballmer who thought he was smarter than he was.
quotes.quote: This is the story of a smart man in Steve Ballmer who thought he was smarter than he was. And I say that because he partnered with a company in Aspiration that went bankrupt. It collapsed in fraud. He, I am sure, lost millions of dollars that he was shocked to discover went into the pocket of a guy who is now in federal prison for 14 years, the co-founder of Aspiration, who by the way shows up in the NBA report and in our reporting because something that he attested to was able to be corroborated by three other patterns in separate companies. So Steve Ballmer scammed, but also was trying to deceive the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Aspiration Fund Advisor LLC's role in the Kawhi Leonard deal
quotes.excerpt: People were taking notes on a conspiracy. And this is going in all directions.
quotes.quote: Kawhi calls it Aspiration in the LLC name, Aspiration is its formal title. The thing that we need to highlight though is that there are notes. I don't want to quote the wire here, but people were taking notes on a conspiracy. And this is going in all directions. Aspiration, the founder you mentioned who is in federal prison, taking notes, threatening the Clippers: If you don't give us what we want, we're going to tell Kawhi that the deal is off that we have with him, and it's because of you, Steve Ballmer, and the Clippers executives. That was in writing, and it's in writing on the other side. It's the Clippers executives talking to each other.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's questionable decision making regarding Kawhi Leonard's Clippers tenure
quotes.excerpt: Was this man, this billionaire, just fawning over Kawhi Leonard and viewing him as some savior?
quotes.quote: I find it incredulous over this. Steve Ballmer ultimately made that deal with Aspiration. He ultimately closed that deal because they blackmailed him about, oh, we're not going to pay Kawhi Leonard. I can't believe that this man, Kawhi Leonard, had the Clippers at his mercy for years, it appears. How do you explain that part of it to the point where you're Steve Ballmer? Was it just about him thinking he was smarter than everybody else? I can understand the desperation in him trying to build the Intuit Dome and him trying to prevent Kawhi Leonard from getting to the Lakers. Was it one of those situations where, because you had originally did the deed and all of it get him to become a Clipper, you were already at his mercy? Or was this man, this billionaire worth over 150 billion dollars, just fawning over Kawhi Leonard and viewing him as some savior that he clearly was not?

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Allegations of off-the-books payments to Kawhi Leonard and Dennis Robertson
quotes.excerpt: 66 million dollars off the books is what the Clippers provided, enabled, facilitated, funneled to Kawhi Leonard
quotes.quote: Steve Ballmer's problem is not money. He is a unique character in this world, man. His problem is the rules. And so when Dennis Robertson smells that, you have been talking about Dennis Robertson longer than any of us have, I think, on television. When Dennis Robertson and Kawhi Leonard together smell that a guy doesn't worry about the money, he worries about the rules, well, guess what they can help with. And so what you have, by the way, on paper now, a 48 million dollar total value in the Aspiration deal, plus 18 million dollars in these three other companies through 2022. 66 million dollars off the books is what the Clippers provided, enabled, facilitated, funneled to Kawhi Leonard and Dennis Robertson on paper. That's what they were promising them.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA's investigation into the Clippers' salary cap circumvention
quotes.excerpt: They basically said, as long as we have an email that we will create in which it's clear
quotes.quote: You do it through a way that the NBA called a novel misinterpretation of what the rules are. And this is where they thought they were smarter than they were. Among other places, but this one in particular. They basically said, as long as we have an email that we will create in which it's clear that we are introducing a sponsor to a player, but we're not the ones encouraging it, then we can do whatever we want when it comes to getting money from A to B to C. What they did not anticipate, however, is that the people who work at those four companies would start asking questions. They would start, in fact, failing as companies. They would start talking to me. In which the whole thing became revealed to be a paper trail that they wanted you to see.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The $28 million endorsement deal between Kawhi Leonard and Aspiration
quotes.excerpt: Aspiration Fund Advisor LLC allegedly contracted Kawhi for a $28M endorsement.
quotes.quote: Klaw's costly flaw: Aspiration Fund Advisor LLC allegedly contracted Kawhi for a $28M endorsement.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The role of Gillian Zucker in the Clippers' financial dealings
quotes.excerpt: There's another hand, and it's Gillian Zucker, the president of business who left, I cannot stress this enough.
quotes.quote: There's another hand, and it's Gillian Zucker, the president of business who left, I cannot stress this enough, left a paper trail that left no doubt as to what exactly this was: facilitation of funneling money to pay Kawhi Leonard. And that in writing is as indicting and as dispositive, as they say in the law, as anything when it comes to what were they trying to do. And so this is all to say this: Steve Ballmer's at the top, as you pointed out, and he is saying to all of these people who are receiving his money and working for him, this is what we need to do. And those people, on the one hand, yes, try to go and do it, but in the process are so varyingly incompetent or self-interested or, frankly, dishonest, all of it, that they end up being his own undoing.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The history of questionable Clippers deals and payments
quotes.excerpt: There were other LLCs he started the week before that led to other undisclosed payments and ownership shares.
quotes.quote: We know with another paper trail that there were other LLCs he started the week before that led to other undisclosed payments and ownership shares that make the 66 million dollars even larger. And the NBA touched none of that. And so when you get to the actual negotiating settlement table, which is what happened here behind the scenes, the NBA came to Steve Ballmer with an undeniable mountain of evidence that they thought, in their view, I am told, was generous given what they could have also kept looking into. And Steve Ballmer said, I'm not settling. And so here we are.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA's decision not to settle with Steve Ballmer
quotes.excerpt: The NBA did not get a settlement from Steve Ballmer, according to my reporting.
quotes.quote: The NBA did not get a settlement from Steve Ballmer, according to my reporting. They realized that the way this story gets even messier is if Steve Ballmer does what he threatens to do yesterday, right after the ruling drops. He threatens to take them to arbitration. But what Steve Ballmer's very expensive attorneys did not realize, Stephen A., it seems, but that the Adam Silver regime and his lawyers very much did, is that arbitration must be activated by the player. It must be activated by Kawhi Leonard and his union, the NBPA. And so when he gives Kawhi a slap on the wrist and the union, in tandem, agrees, we're going to settle this, Kawhi is going to move on to Toronto, that's our goal here, we've achieved this remarkably light punishment that is beyond, again, any merit because he was so central to the whole story, self-evidently, what they did was they took arbitration off the table and boxed Steve Ballmer in to one last possibility, which is him suing the NBA in real court.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: David Kelley's statement on the investigation into Steve Ballmer
quotes.excerpt: Retroactively punishing the Clippers for violating a rule that never existed is hardly consistent with due process.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: Let's read Steve Ballmer's attorney's statement, David Kelley. This is what he wrote: 'Mr. Ballmer's reputation has been irreparably damaged as he now finds himself embroiled not only in this heavily biased investigation, but in civil litigation, the Aspiration bankruptcy proceeding, and more. Retroactively punishing the Clippers for violating a rule that never existed is hardly consistent with due process.' Before I get back to Kawhi Leonard, your reaction to that statement directly?

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo Torre
text_blocks.text: I think he needs more people, as they say. He has been saying this whole time that there is an explanation for how all this happened, and for a year, he has offered nothing. In fact, the opposite has happened. There has been documentation and sourcing and testimony, some of it transcribed by hand by Lawrence Frank, others of it confessed in this slap on the wrist settlement with Kawhi Leonard, that in fact is exactly what it looked like. And Kawhi says, 'I regret that people in my inner circle did not abide by...' blah, blah, blah, blah, blah. But the point is, they all say, 'Yeah, this happened.' That's the upshot of it.
